skills.name: Belgian Congo: consequences and the limits of intervention

note.text: The Congo crisis disrupted administration and economic activity, displaced people and intensified conflict over national leadership and territorial unity. Prime Minister Patrice Lumumba was killed in 1961. ONUC operated from July 1960 to June 1964, with a mandate that developed during the crisis. Katanga was reintegrated, but political instability did not simply disappear. Mobutu seized power in 1965. Distinguish an operation’s specific achievements from a claim that it settled every later conflict.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to explain political and human effects while distinguishing ONUC’s task from a complete solution. Builds on: independence, mutiny and secession in the Congo crisis. Leads to: Portuguese transitions and comparative instability.

sections.heading: Explain the history
sections.text: The Congo crisis disrupted administration and economic activity, displaced people and intensified conflict over national leadership and territorial unity. Prime Minister Patrice Lumumba was killed in {1961}. ONUC operated from July {1960} to June {1964}, with a mandate that developed during the crisis. Katanga was reintegrated, but political instability did not simply disappear. Mobutu seized power in {1965}. Distinguish an operation’s specific achievements from a claim that it settled every later conflict.

sections.heading: Follow the evidence and examples
sections.text: UN accounts describe efforts concerning territorial integrity, foreign military elements and the prevention of wider civil war. Human suffering and political rivalry outlasted a single resolution. Later centralisation under Mobutu was not the same event as independence in {1960}. This lesson concerns the early post-independence Congo crisis, not every later war in today’s Democratic Republic of the Congo.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify actor, action, place and period before explaining a relationship. Use the practice text only for the claim it supports. Distinguish a cause, an event and an outcome; compare authentic sources before treating an interpretation as established. A sequence alone does not prove that every later outcome was inevitable.

violent conflict over the new state’s political leadership
specific international action without a guarantee of permanent peace

cards.idea: Connect a specific action or event to the historical feature it illustrates.
example: Conflict displaced people and interrupted administration and economic activity.
Lumumba was killed in {1961} during the wider crisis.
Katanga’s reintegration did not eliminate every later political conflict.
Mobutu seized power in {1965}, after the initial independence crisis.

cards.idea: Check a claim against the sequence, setting and limits of the evidence.
example: Civil conflict affects only the wording of constitutional documents. Correction: Its consequences extend to people and livelihoods.
Lumumba’s death occurred before the Congo gained independence. Correction: The killing followed independence in {1960}.
ONUC’s withdrawal proved all future Congolese instability had ended. Correction: A mandate and a period of intervention have limits.
Mobutu’s {1965} seizure and June {1960} independence were the same event. Correction: They were distinct events in different years.
